title: They didn’t reject Jesus.
paragraphs:
They didn’t reject Jesus.
They redesigned Him.

And the scariest part?
It still feels like faith.

You can sing the songs.
Post the verses.
Say “God is good.”

And still be following a version of Jesus…
that never touches your sin.

That never confronts your pride.
That never asks you to change.

And now the question is sitting in your chest—
quiet, but heavy:
What if the Jesus I believe in… isn’t the real Jesus?

Because it’s possible to love a version of Christ
that never existed.

To build a Savior in your own image—
soft where you want softness,
silent where you need silence,
absent where obedience feels costly.
We don’t usually say it out loud.
But we edit Him.

We remove the hard sayings.
We skip the uncomfortable commands.
We highlight the blessings…
and bury the call to surrender.

And slowly—without realizing—
we turn discipleship into preference.

Not transformation.
Not repentance.
Not a cross.
Just comfort.
Just control.
Just a Jesus who agrees with us.
But Scripture doesn’t give us that option.
In Matthew 16:24, Jesus says:
“If anyone would come after Me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow Me.”

Not admire.
Not adjust.
Not negotiate.

Deny.
Take up.
Follow.

This is not behavior modification.
This is death to self.

Some scholars interpret “take up your cross” as a metaphor for daily surrender—
a willingness to lay down your will, your desires, your identity,
and trust fully in Christ.

But make no mistake—
the cross was not comfortable.

It was not symbolic to them.
It meant suffering.
It meant loss.
It meant everything.
And Jesus didn’t soften that truth.
He intensified it.
In Luke 9:23, He says:
“If anyone would come after Me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow Me.”
Daily.

Not once.
Not when it’s easy.
Not when it aligns with your plans.
Daily surrender.
And this is where many quietly walk away.

Not loudly.
Not dramatically.
Just slowly.
“After this many of His disciples turned back and no longer walked with Him.”
Why?
Because His words got hard.

Because the real Jesus
doesn’t bend to our desires.
He exposes them.

He confronts the parts of us
we’ve been hiding behind filters and good behavior.

The pride we defend.
The secret sin we excuse.
The bitterness we protect.
The habits we refuse to surrender.

And suddenly—
the Jesus who once felt comforting
now feels confronting.
And we have a choice.
Do we reshape Him to fit our life?
Or do we surrender our life to follow Him?
Because here’s the truth that hits deep:

If your Jesus never corrects you…
you’re not being discipled.

If your Jesus never calls you higher…
you’re not being transformed.

If your Jesus never leads you to repentance…
you’re not experiencing grace the way Scripture defines it.
Because grace is not permission to stay the same.
Grace is power to be made new.
Titus 2:11–12 says:
“For the grace of God has appeared… training us to renounce ungodliness and worldly passions, and to live self-controlled, upright, and godly lives.”

Grace doesn’t ignore sin.
It trains you to leave it.

Grace doesn’t excuse your darkness.
It pulls you out of it.
But here’s where everything shifts.
Here’s the part many miss.
Jesus is not calling you to die… without first dying for you.

Before He ever said, “take up your cross,”
He carried His.

Before He called you to surrender,
He surrendered everything.

On that cross—
He didn’t edit His love for you.
He didn’t soften His sacrifice.

He took the full weight of your sin—
every hidden thought,
every secret habit,
every version of you that tried to run from God—
and He paid for it in full.
Romans 5:8 says:
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”

Not when you got it together.
Not when you cleaned up your life.
While you were still in it.

That version of you—
the one you’re ashamed of—
the one you hide—
the one you hope no one ever sees—
He saw it.
And He still chose the cross.
This is the real Jesus.

Holy enough to confront your sin.
Loving enough to forgive it.
Powerful enough to break it.

And now He stands—not with condemnation—
but with invitation.
Not to a better version of yourself.
But to a brand new life.
2 Corinthians 5:17 says:
“Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come.”

Not edited.
Not improved.
New.

But you don’t get resurrection
without surrender.

You don’t get new life
while holding onto the old one.
So here’s the moment.
Right here.

No performance.
No pretending.
Just honesty.

Have you been following Jesus…
or just a version of Him that fits your comfort?
And if the Holy Spirit is pressing on something right now—
That tension you feel?
That’s not shame trying to crush you.
That’s conviction trying to free you.
Jesus is not asking you to be perfect.
He’s asking you to come.

To repent.
To lay it down.
To stop editing Him—
and start following Him.
For real.
And here’s the beauty—
You’re not too far gone.
You’re not too broken.
You’re not too inconsistent.
Grace is still reaching.
Mercy is still calling.
The cross is still enough.
So come back.

Not to a comfortable Jesus—
but to the real One.
The One who loves you too much to leave you the same.

If this is you—
don’t stay silent.
Let this be your moment of surrender.
who’s been following a filtered version of Jesus.
because you’ll need this reminder again.
